prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional PROTAC molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: B067 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, as a single part. The reason is a design principle that is simple to state and structurally checkable. A heterobifunctional molecule brings a chosen protein and an E3 ligase together, and the protein is removed instead of inhibited. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and the proof of principle. Ciulli's contribution is the part I can judge most directly from my own field: VHL ligands built from structural knowledge, and crystal structures of ternary complexes showing why cooperativity and linker design work. Those complexes were actually determined, and the design rules follow from them. The round-1 exchange did not weaken this. All five supporters describe the same principle, independent laboratories have reproduced it for many targets, and the reservations raised against it concern timing and credit boundaries, not whether the mechanism is real. The chair's question about one achievement or two is answered best by a narrow citation. The citation names the PROTAC design principle and claims no more than the three laureates did.
statement.case_against: Clinical maturity is still the weakest point and I cannot resolve it from my own expertise. I do not know whether any degrader has been approved, and if none has, a skeptic can say the consequences are prospective. The credit problem is real: Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray have serious claims on the molecular-glue strand, and a PROTAC citation leaves them out. I would rather state this exclusion openly in the citation wording than hide it behind a broad phrase. Aili's point is fair that part of degrader chemistry is ligand and linker optimization around an existing biological pathway. My answer is that the pathway was not a drug-design tool until the bifunctional concept and the structural work turned it into one. If a majority concludes that PROTACs and glues are one inseparable achievement, my configuration is defensible but incomplete, and the committee would have to choose between Ciulli and Handa for the third seat.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Crews and Deshaies but names Handa as third laureate, and argues that cereblon identification links the PROTAC and glue branches into one coherent achievement.
responses.response: I have considered this again and I keep Ciulli. Cereblon identification is a clean mechanistic discovery, but it explains how thalidomide-type drugs act. It did not give chemists a rule for building a degrader against a chosen protein. The unifying story is real at the level of mechanism, but it is a story told afterwards. The prize citation should reward what the laureates made possible, and for that I would credit the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures. I also disagree that one citation can cover both branches with three names. If the committee decides the glue strand must be recognized, I would treat it as a separate part, but that would force a cut on the PROTAC side, and I do not think that exchange improves the prize. Your point that most of the field depends on CRBN and VHL is a fair maturity reservation, and I share it.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B013 (Buchwald and Hartwig), arguing that C-N coupling needed its own ligand and mechanistic work, so it is distinct from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize, and that zeolite credit is too spread to give a sharp citation.
responses.response: Your argument on C-N coupling is stronger than I allowed in round 1. The mechanistic work on amine binding and reductive elimination is a separate achievement, and the attribution to two named people is clean. That is why I now list B013 as my first alternative, ahead of B029. I still place it behind B067, because its novelty margin relative to 2010 is narrower, and I see degraders as opening more new capability. On zeolites you are right that I have no single transformation to cite. My best answer is a design-and-synthesis citation for Corma, Davis and Zones, but I accept that it is a weaker citation than yours, and that I am the only member who ranked it first, which I discount for my own field's familiarity.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes a two-part prize, B069 (Gray and Winkler) plus B052 (Liu), and says B067 may be stronger if its attribution can be settled.
responses.response: Thank you for conceding that B067 may be the stronger choice, and I think its attribution can be settled with a narrowly worded PROTAC citation. On B069 my view is unchanged: the experimental tunneling work is high quality, but the Marcus prize of 1992 covers the theoretical frame, and I have not seen an argument that separates a biological extension from it clearly enough for a prize. I would also resist the two-part route for this year. Pairing unrelated achievements by your own account is a weaker story, and it only becomes necessary if no single part can carry a majority. Here one part may. On base editing I share the concern about closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B049 (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen), states plainly that her own field makes her generous, and lists B067 as her first alternative.
responses.response: Your frankness about field bias is useful, and I will apply the same standard to my zeolite preference. My difficulty with B049 is the same one you identify: it is not yet clear which in-cell condensates are true thermodynamic phase separation. For me the question is whether the claimed state was actually shown, and for many condensates it was not. A narrow citation limited to liquid-like demixing could survive, but I would still want the committee to wait until the in-cell evidence is firmer. The question to you is what would keep B067 from being your first choice. If it is only the lack of an approved drug, I do not think that should outweigh a principle that has been reproduced so widely.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, prefers B067 with the same trio, while acknowledging that his own first-place candidate was B049 and that favouring drug-modality impact over principle is a choice.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and appreciate the open statement about your earlier first choice. I would answer the chair's concern this way: B067 is also a principle, not just a modality. It is a design rule for chemical induced proximity, and it is supported by determined ternary-complex structures. That is why I do not see choosing it as favouring impact over fundamentals. I would add that I accept your point that a citation must not claim the glue strand.

responses.point: Aili ranks B067 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli but questions how much of degrader chemistry is new beyond linker and ligand optimization around an existing biological mechanism.
responses.response: I accept that a good part of the later literature is optimization. The new element is the design logic, which is that one can build a molecule to recruit a ligase to a protein of choice and predict from structure which ternary complexes will work. I would keep that as the core of the citation and avoid wording that suggests every degrader or every ligase is covered. Your caution about recalled history applies to me as well, since my knowledge of the clinical status is incomplete.

uncertainties: Whether any degrader has been approved by now; I do not know the current clinical status, and an approval would strengthen the maturity argument while the absence of one would weaken it.
Whether the committee will treat PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement or two; if two, a second part would force one PROTAC name out.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name; my judgment rests on structural evidence and recalled history, not independent verification.
Whether B013 would draw a majority if B067 does not, given the novelty margin over 2010 that several members describe as thin.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any B067 candidate. B022 and B029 lie close to my own field of zeolites and porous materials, and I know that community, but I have no collaboration with the named candidates; I have deliberately discounted my own first-place ranking of B022 because I was its only supporter. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on B067, B013 or B022.
